title: Research
text:
My research interests lie at the intersection of statistical learning, deep learning, time-series forecasting, and quantitative finance.
My earlier work focused on computer vision and lightweight deep-learning models. My current research studies attention mechanisms in nonlinear time series and probabilistic forecasting for financial markets.

Integrating Convexity and DeepLabv3+ for Semantic Segmentation of Power Lines
Ying Hou, Jindou Tuo, Haochen Li, Zhuoxin Yan, Xuemei Huang, and Yuqi Wang.
Research Square Preprint, 2026.
This paper proposes PLE-DeepLabv3+, a lightweight semantic-segmentation model for detecting thin and low-contrast power lines in complex aerial imagery. The model combines a reconfigured ConvNeXtV2 backbone, direction-selective coordinate attention, efficient multi-scale feature fusion, adaptive edge detection, and a class-aware focal loss.

Manuscripts in Preparation

When Does Softmax Attention Outperform Linear Prediction in Nonlinear Time Series?
Haochen Li
Manuscript in preparation.
This project studies the statistical conditions under which nonlinear softmax attention can outperform classical linear prediction in nonlinear autoregressive time series.
The central mechanism is a trade-off between the approximation advantage of attention and its additional statistical estimation and search complexity. The analysis develops signal-complexity thresholds characterizing when the benefits of nonlinear attention become large enough to justify its greater complexity.
The project also investigates approximate representability, projection gain, multi-head attention, temporal dependence, and the empirical transition between linear and attention-based prediction.


Replication and Cross-Asset Extension of the Intraday Volume Estimator
Haochen Li
Manuscript based on my UCL MSc dissertation, currently being prepared for submission.
This project replicates and extends a Transformer-based probabilistic intraday volume estimator. The original framework is evaluated on U.S. equities and subsequently extended to G10 foreign-exchange markets.
The model produces probabilistic forecasts through a Student-t predictive distribution and incorporates asset embeddings, intraday temporal features, and multi-step training. The study also investigates extensions from trading volume to intraday volatility and market activity.
A central part of the project examines whether improvements in statistical forecasting accuracy translate into economically meaningful execution benefits. The empirical analysis compares ex-post and fully causal scheduling procedures and evaluates their performance against historical intraday volume curves.
A revised manuscript based on the dissertation is currently being developed for submission.

title: Research
text:
Current Research Directions
My current work focuses on the following questions:

When does softmax attention outperform linear prediction in nonlinear time series?
Which nonlinear structures and signal regimes justify the additional complexity of attention?
How do multi-head attention and temporal encoding affect statistical efficiency?
When do Transformer models outperform linear, tree-based, and recurrent baselines in financial forecasting?
Can improvements in probabilistic volume and volatility forecasts produce economically meaningful gains in trading and execution?

title: Haochen (Jerry) Li
text:
I am an M.S. student in Statistical Science at Duke University. Before joining Duke, I studied Computational Finance and Mathematics with Economics at University College London.
My research interests lie in the theory and applications of deep learning, with a particular focus on time-series forecasting.
